findings.evidence: Folder selected must be of type the database can read and that is “name”.kdb
findings.rationale: No behaviour is stated when a non-.kdb file is selected; also 'Folder' is used where a database file is meant, which could be misread.

findings.evidence: or else the previews one will be replace if selected
findings.rationale: It is unclear what 'the previous one' and 'if selected' refer to (which database, selected by whom/for what).

findings.evidence: All data related to the word must be shown
findings.rationale: 'Related to the word' is unbounded: which fields are searched (title, URL, notes...) and match rules (substring, case) are not defined beyond one example.

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the new group/subgroup to be created
findings.rationale: No behaviour is specified when the user tries to create a group/subgroup with an empty name.

findings.evidence: A name is required in order for the group/subgroup to be renamed
findings.rationale: No behaviour is specified when the rename is attempted with an empty name.

findings.evidence: Password field and repeat password field must be identical
findings.rationale: The system response to a mismatch (error message, blocking save) is not stated.

findings.evidence: the repeat password field must be Changed and be identical with password field
findings.rationale: Restates KP-012/KP-013 (repeat field must be completed and identical) with no distinct behaviour.

findings.evidence: Sequence’s length must not be more than a line (59 characters)
findings.rationale: What happens when an Auto-Type sequence exceeds 59 characters (rejected, truncated, warning) is not stated.

findings.evidence: Only one database file is allowed in command line options
findings.rationale: Behaviour when more than one database file is passed on the command line is not specified.

findings.evidence: File formats are not specialized password database formats
findings.rationale: It is not stated which file formats (import/export? which ones?) the statement applies to.
The file formats in scope are not identified.

findings.evidence: The format for service information description is defined
findings.rationale: Verbatim repeat of PE-001.

findings.evidence: any resource failure will be reported
findings.rationale: Who reports resource failures and to whom is not stated.

findings.evidence: The interaction protocol between Web Server-SR, SR-mediator is defined.
findings.rationale: Verbatim repeat of PE-003.
'Malicious' is not defined; no criteria for detection are given.
The component responsible for detecting and rejecting requests is not identified.
Which content is 'necessary' is not defined.
'Considered' does not specify what the system must do with anticipated and unanticipated requests; not testable.

findings.evidence: The format for service information description is defined
findings.rationale: Verbatim repeat of PE-001.
'Malicious' is undefined (same issue accepted for PE-007).
'acted upon' gives no resulting behaviour (compare 'rejected' in PE-007).

findings.evidence: Malicious requests are identified and acted upon.
findings.rationale: Near-restatement of PE-007; additionally 'acted upon' is weaker than 'rejected', leaving the intended action unclear.
'Sufficient' has no threshold.
Which policies are 'functional' is undefined; requirement is not verifiable.
'Effective' has no measurable criterion.

findings.evidence: Policies are in place to perform renegotiation for problem resolution.
findings.rationale: Verbatim repeat of PE-023.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Restates GJ-003 (SQL based database).

findings.evidence: Shall install online help for users
findings.rationale: No subject: unclear whether the system or the developers install the online help.

findings.evidence: Shall deliver Operations and Maintenance manual
findings.rationale: No subject identifying who delivers the documentation.

findings.evidence: email customer and vendor in less than 1 second
findings.rationale: The triggering event for the email (order placed, shipped, etc.) and its starting point for the 1-second timing are not stated.

findings.evidence: validate credit card in less than 2 seconds
findings.rationale: No behaviour is defined when card validation fails or the validation service is unavailable.
Backup period/frequency is not given.
No behaviour specified when a card is flagged as fraudulent or the validation service fails.
Which information counts as 'sensitive' is not defined.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks and block IP automatically
findings.rationale: Detection criteria/threshold and block duration/unblocking are not specified.
No number of attempts and no resulting action (lockout, alert, duration) is stated.

findings.evidence: validate 'existing' credit card in system after each log in
findings.rationale: Behaviour when the stored card is invalid or expired is not stated.

findings.evidence: image files that are too large in size
findings.rationale: No size threshold defines 'too large' (nor target size).
Behaviour when the email address does not exist or cannot be verified is not stated.
Subjective, no measurable usability criterion.
Subjective, no measurable learnability criterion.
Subjective, no testable criterion.

findings.evidence: friend easy to read error messages
findings.rationale: 'Friendly'/'easy to read' are subjective.
'Clear' is subjective and the symbol/color scheme is not defined.
What plugins and what 'interchangeable' means are not defined.
Subjective, no measurable maintainability criterion.
Subjective, no measurable criterion.
'Extremely portable' is unquantified.

findings.evidence: easy to migrate or backed up
findings.rationale: Subjective, no measurable criterion.
'Weborder system' is a new name for the product called 'Web Store' elsewhere.

findings.evidence: shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection
findings.rationale: Who fixes and patches the hardware is not stated (and hardware patching is unclear).
Lists Apache web server as the OS, conflicting with GJ-002 which specifies Slackware Linux 2.6 as the OS and Apache as the web server.

findings.evidence: lock a Member account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts
findings.rationale: Specifies the lockout trigger but omits the lockout duration and unlock/error behavior.
Ambiguous pronoun 'him' could refer to the Librarian, the Member, or the Guarantor.
Uses placeholder 'TBD' instead of a concrete expiration duration.

findings.evidence: user-friendly ... easy to navigate ... loads rapidly
findings.rationale: Subjective, unmeasurable usability and performance terms without quantitative criteria.
Maximum renewal count is left as TBD.

findings.evidence: validate item eligibility ... and issue the loan receipt
findings.rationale: Omits error handling when the barcode is invalid or the item is ineligible for checkout.

findings.evidence: the allowed maximum number of active hold requests
findings.rationale: Fails to specify the numeric maximum hold limit.

findings.evidence: borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously
findings.rationale: Conflicts with SD-009, which limits active simultaneous loans to at most 5 items.
Conflicts with SD-010, which defines the standard loan duration as 14 calendar days.

findings.evidence: self-register online ... and immediately check out physical books without Librarian ID verification
findings.rationale: Directly contradicts SD-001, which requires in-person Librarian verification of a government-issued photo ID before account creation.

findings.evidence: remain held indefinitely until the requesting Member explicitly cancels
findings.rationale: Directly contradicts SD-011, which mandates automatic cancellation after 72 hours.

findings.evidence: and/or suspend borrowing privileges and/or apply a penalty flag
findings.rationale: Multiple 'and/or' coordinations leave unclear which subset of actions is mandatory.

findings.evidence: shall be reviewed, approved, and recorded
findings.rationale: Passive construction omits the authorized actor responsible for reviewing and approving waivers.
Weak conditional phrase 'if appropriate' leaves trigger conditions and timing undefined.
Retention period is marked as TBD instead of a concrete number of years.

findings.evidence: $1.25 USD per overdue day ... with no maximum cap
findings.rationale: Conflicts with SD-019, which specifies $0.50 USD per day capped at $20.00 USD.

findings.evidence: renew borrowed items online at any time regardless of any unpaid overdue fine balance
findings.rationale: Directly contradicts SD-020, which blocks renewals when unpaid fines exceed $5.00 USD.
Uses 'Patron' instead of the established SRS term 'Member' defined in SD-001 and SD-009.
Unquantified terms 'quickly' and 'many users' lack measurable latency and concurrency thresholds.
Weak phrase 'where possible' makes the requirement non-verifiable and optional without criteria.
Vague qualifiers 'sufficient' and 'acceptable' provide no testable acceptance threshold.
Vague terms 'efficiently', 'large', and 'noticeable' lack concrete volume and latency bounds.
States that the system detects active references but omits what action/consequence follows (block, warn, or cascade).
Backup frequency is unspecified (TBD).
Multiple vague terms leave event scope, latency, and retention period undefined.

findings.evidence: unreachable for more than 10 seconds, the Failover Manager shall log event FAILOVER-01
findings.rationale: Omits the recovery action/timeout when primary database failover occurs.
Vague terms 'adequate' and 'clear' lack concrete protocol and error-format specifications.
Conflicts with SD-002, which requires Member passwords of at least 12 characters.
Conflicts with SD-004, which terminates inactive sessions after 15 minutes.

findings.evidence: reversible AES-256 encryption so Administrators can decrypt and retrieve forgotten passwords
findings.rationale: Directly contradicts SD-003, which mandates one-way bcrypt hashing and forbids storing recoverable passwords.
